items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-04-07
items.q: I was supporting my brother. I was supporting the band, you see.

ctx.x: Yeah, that's Tasso's right. He was the leader of that man. But that was a wonderful drummer, he was the leader. Ace man. And he had timpani, and bells, and chimes, he had everything. And, well I was pretty, a fellow would always, it sounds something, and the bass drum had a beautiful sound. So I'd carry it. Right now, in my grip, I got all my music paper, you know, doing my trance, you know, arranging. I've got, still got a guitar tuner. That's how I catch things, you know. And you know what I used to do…

items.title: Joseph Rene Interview, 1960-09-08
items.q: And my brother wouldn't play without me, you know. He didn't even want to play on a lot of other drums, you see. Because he knew what I was going to do. And you see, all he had to do was look at me and I knew what he wanted, you see.

ctx.x: And he wanted to get some old music together, you see. And he wanted some jazz. So Santiago told him, saying, I wanted the most little jazzy fella we knowed around here. And he started around there, way around Budapetite time, you see. It was right there, you see. And my brother wouldn't play without me, you know. He didn't even want to play on a lot of other drums, you see. Because he knew what I was going to do. And you see, all he had to do was look at me and I knew what he wanted, you see. items.title: Joseph Rene and Edna Kelly Interview, 1969-12-15
items.q: I was going to leave my brother, you know. We had such, you know, good, wonderful band.

ctx.x: And that's John Forkartin. Who was drumming with him? Well, he had, of course in the late years he had Joe Watkins. Who? Joe Watkins. Joe Watkins. Well, he was a much more recent drummer. You probably don't even remember him. Yeah, no. He died fairly recently.

Yeah, yeah. Well, there's another fella. I can't think of his name. He had a drummer. He tried to get me with him and I said, no, I wouldn't. I was going to leave my brother, you know. We had such, you know, good, wonderful band. I guess you must have heard.
I talked about it. Did you stay more or less continually playing with your brother all the time?
